text:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected — p99 latency > 3.0s for /v1/generate (cluster: gpu-prod-1). Alert ID: A-1799802468. Autoscaler: OK, error rate: low, streaming stalls observed.

anya (oncall): saw it, paging in. I'm grabbing metrics now. p95 ~ 820ms, p99 jumped to 3.2s across the last 3 minutes. Streaming stall traces show long gaps during first 8-32 token windows.

mike (perf): linked chart: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/latency/gpu-prod-1?from=-15m - looks correlated to small subset of pods on node gpu-node-17. p50 stable. Tail shows spikes aligned with NVML clock changes.

david (infra): checking node health. Running quick checks:
```
ssh root@gpu-node-17 "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,temperature.gpu,clocks.current.sm,clocks.current.memory,utilization.gpu,retired_pending_rows,retired_pages,voltage" --format=csv
```
Output snippet: 
```
index, temperature.gpu, clocks.current.sm, clocks.current.memory, utilization.gpu, retired_pending_rows
0, 92, 405, 2505, 99, 0
1, 87, 405, 2505, 97, 12
```
There are increasing ECC corrected error counts on GPU 1, and nv-hostengine logs show repeated "GPU has been reset due to thermal throttling" messages.

anya (oncall): if GPU is resetting/clocks dropping that's likely causing long stalls for streams since KV cache invalidations + recompile. Can we cordon and drain that node?

david (infra): I'll cordon+drain. Plan: cordon gpu-node-17, evict pods with graceful 30s, prefer migrate to gpu-node-09/10. Start drain now.

ops-bot: Command run: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17` :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Command run: `kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30` :in_progress:

mike (perf): quick mitigation option: route traffic away from heavy streaming routes to CPU fallback model variant (model-lite) to reduce pressure on GPU pool. Jess can notify customers about temporary degradation.

jess (support): I'll draft customer note. Which tenants impacted? I see a spike for tenant: AcmeMedia (prod) and a couple of low-volume customers. P99 is affecting streaming sessions, some clients saw stall >5s. Sending interim status now. :loudspeaker:

anya (oncall): After drain started, p99 dropped from 3.2s down to ~1.1s in 90s as pods rescheduled. Good sign. But node still shows kernel dmesg entries for ECC: `GPU 0000:65:00.0: Corrected ECC error` increasing. Suggest hardware replacement for that GPU.

mike (perf): timeline notes:
- 00:00 alert triggered (p99 > 3s)
- +00:02 identified gpu-node-17 as common denominator
- +00:04 cordon/drain initiated
- +00:05 p99 trending down, but intermittent stalls for existing long-running sessions remain until reconnect.

jess (support): Customer update sent to AcmeMedia: "We're investigating intermittent streaming stalls in a subset of GPU nodes. We're migrating workloads and expect reduced latency within minutes. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA for hardware replacement."

david (infra): Rebooting node after drain to clear GPU state and force hardware diagnostics. Command: `ssh root@gpu-node-17 sudo reboot`. Will open HW ticket with vendor (NV-INC-2026-045).

ops-bot: Node removed from service: gpu-node-17 cordoned and drained.

anya (oncall): handoff plan: I'll keep monitoring for 15m then hand to jess for overnight watch. Please attach logs to internal incident: INC-2026-0987 and link perf dashboards + dmesg/ECC outputs.

mike (perf): adding short-term alert tuning: trigger on NVML clock drops > 20% across p99 path and ECC corrected errors > 5 in 5m on any single GPU. Also creating dashboard panel for streaming stalls correlated with NVML resets.

david (infra): hardware notes to ticket: ECC corrected errors increasing; thermal readings peaked at 92C; vendor suggests GPU will be replaced. Recommend RMA for GPU index 1 on gpu-node-17.

jess (support): marking customers impacted: [AcmeMedia-prod], [BetaApp-prod], [internal-systems]. Notifying account teams.

anya (oncall): current status: p95=600ms, p99=1.1s, error rate normal, no new NVML resets after drain. Marking incident as mitigated. Will keep incident channel open for postmortem items and hardware replacement coordination.

mike (perf): follow-ups: 1) run long-run streaming test against node pool with induced thermal stress to validate fallback behavior, 2) add automatic fallback route to model-lite if node-level resets exceed threshold, 3) compute cost/latency tradeoff for earlier routing fallback.

david (infra): RMA ticket created NV-RMA-7092. Schedule swap during low-traffic window.

jess (support): leaving note for handoff: I'll watch overnight and escalate if p99 > 1.5s for more than 3 minutes.

anya (oncall): handing over to jess in 10. Thanks all :raised_hands: Summary for postmortem: cause - flaky GPU with escalating ECC corrected errors + thermal events -> NVML resets -> streaming stalls and KV cache invalidations -> p99 SLO breach. Mitigation - cordon+drain, reboot, migrate workloads, customer notifications. Next steps - RMA + alert tuning + perf tests.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0987 updated with mitigation notes and linked logs.

jess (support): acknowledged handoff. I'll post final update in 30m or earlier if anything changes.

[END THREAD]
